statement: No peer input can halt a Runtime: malformed, stale or racing input is refused, and only a broken local invariant halts.

layers.contract: n/a: what a Runtime does with a peer input is off-chain; the chain halts nothing of the Runtime
layers.rig: owed: test rig (a walk predicate for this rule; none is named yet)

killers.name: halt-on-refusal
full-halts
bad-halts
R-X1 no peer input halts the Runtime: strangers, stale acks and repeats are refused in place
R-X1 an input for an Entity this Runtime does not host is refused with notice, as a row
R-X1 a message from a stranger is refused with notice and changes nothing
R-DURABLE R-X1 in every world: no halt, no leak, every WAL replays, equal heads mean equal states
R-DURABLE R-X1 every run settles; nothing halts or leaves ahead of its disk, with junk hashes and ids
R-X1 planted bug: a recovery that forgets the last row does not replay to what the Host holds
R-X1 a message for an Entity this Host does not host is refused in place, and queues nothing
R-X1 a forged ack, a future frame and a stranger's message are rows with notices, never a halt
R-X1 one input queued three times is three inputs: the third stays queued
R-X1 a row refused for an Entity the Runtime does not host asks nothing of the chain
R-X1 a text nested thousands deep is a fault, not a stack overflow, and the bound is exact
R-X1 a value nested past the bound is refused at the write: no row is stored that cannot be read
R-X1 a bigint of hundreds of thousands of digits is a fault, not a throw, and the bound is exact
R-X1 a bigint past the bound is refused at the write: no row is stored that cannot be read
R-X1 a frame with a bigint of hundreds of thousands of digits is refused, not thrown, link lives
R-X1 a hello, a reply and a finish nested thousands deep or far over the bound are refused, not thrown
R-X1 a text nested thousands deep, or far over the bound, is refused before anything is believed
R-X1 a tx tag that every object has is no message: refused, and the link still hears the next record
R-X1 a tx tag that is a property of every object is a wrong shape, never a thrown error
R-X1 lines arrive whole and in order, and a write that holds a newline is two lines
R-X1 a line over the bound is cut off, and a peer that goes away ends the read
R-X1 a port nobody listens on is a fault the caller reads, not a throw
